residents.about: I moved into Rose Cottage last spring and became the city's community gardener. Reading in my armchair with a cup of tea is my favourite way to unwind.
I ran the local post office for forty years, so I know everyone's comings and goings. Since I retired I miss the chatter at the counter; a good natter on the pond bench helps.
I moved to Tiny City a month ago to set up the repair workshop. I'd rather fix a squeaky gate than make small talk, but I'm trying to meet people.
I took over the general store from my aunt; I know what everyone buys before they ask. I like everything in its place: tins lined up, labels facing out.
I trained as a chef downtown and came home to cook at the neighbourhood café. My soup of the day is never the same twice, and I'm proud of that.
Serving at the café means I hear all the city news first. I paint watercolours on my days off and dream of a little exhibition.
I'm up before everyone else to bake the neighbourhood's bread; the bakery was my grandmother's. I go for a run along the fitness trail whenever my legs aren't covered in flour.
I've been the city doctor for twenty years; I've stitched up half the neighbourhood at some point. Evenings with a medical journal and a pot of tea suit me fine.
I left school last summer, and I've just got my first proper job: running the neon bar in the evenings. Money's tight, so I make the most of free things: the park, the trail, a chat.
I've lived in Tiny City all my eighty-two years and remember when the pond was a well. My knees aren't what they were, but a cup of coffee at the café keeps me cheerful.
I run the Pulse Gym's early shift; there's nothing like an empty gym at seven in the morning. I moved into Skyline Tower for the view, and I'm still learning everyone's names.
I hand out the shoes at Strike Lanes and know every regular's size by heart. I love a busy room and a loud laugh; quiet evenings make me restless.
I look after the Pixel Arcade, and I hold the high score on two of its machines. I'm better with machines than with people, but I'm working on it.
I run the cue club in the evenings; I've played pool since I could see over the table. A good game of snooker settles any argument, as far as I'm concerned.
I retired from the railways and moved into Birch Cottage to be near the park. A morning by the pond with a fishing rod is my idea of a good day.
